text:
The Maple Leafs climbed back from 3-1 down, tied it 4:11 into the third, and held the tie for 51 seconds. Gabriel Landeskog's second goal of the night restored Colorado's lead, the Avalanche scored twice more late, and Toronto lost 6-3 for its fourth straight defeat. After Auston Matthews called out his teammates following the loss to New Jersey, and with the coaching rumors growing louder, this was the kind of night that makes a bad week feel worse.

Toronto started well. Darren Raddysh scored from the point 3:33 in, a slap shot with under a 1% chance, Matthews and Jack Roslovic assisting. Colorado answered with two goals 77 seconds apart late in the first: Brock Nelson off a T.J. Hughes feed, then Landeskog on a backhand from close in, set up by Nicolas Roy and Cale Makar, who had shaken off the injury scare and played 23 minutes. Devon Toews made it 3-1 early in the second on another 1% chance.

The Leafs' kids pulled them back in. Easton Cowan scored with 29 seconds left in the second, with rookie Gavin McKenna picking up an assist, and Cowan then set up Roslovic's tying backhand early in the third. That goal took Toronto's win chance from 25% to 52%. Then Landeskog beat Sergei Bobrovsky again, Nazem Kadri and Sam Malinski assisting, and Colorado's chance jumped to 76%. Mackenzie Blackwood's best save came on Roslovic, a 21% look late in the third, the stop that added most to Colorado's night. Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas then scored 15 seconds apart to finish it.

Landeskog's shooting had been the quiet worry of Colorado's start, and this was the clearest sign yet that it's coming back. Toews and Makar were on the ice for 2.29 and 2.61 expected goals (the quality of chances) for.

For Toronto, the numbers are not kind. Colorado had 3.65 expected goals to 2.49 and by our replay deserved this 61% of the time. Bobrovsky allowed 1.9 goals more than his shots deserved. The Leafs won the first meeting, 6-3 in October. A month later the same score points the other way, and the questions in Toronto are getting harder to answer.
headline: Landeskog answers the tie, and Toronto's slide hits four
